introduction.en: The financial market is broadly divided into the money market and the capital market, serving distinct roles in the economy based on the maturity of financial instruments.
introduction.hi: The financial market is broadly divided into the money market and the capital market, serving distinct roles in the economy based on the maturity of financial instruments.

body.en: The money market, regulated by the RBI, deals with short-term funds (up to one year) and provides liquidity to banks and corporations. In contrast, the capital market, regulated by SEBI, facilitates long-term investment through equity and debt instruments. While the money market ensures the smooth functioning of daily cash flows, the capital market enables long-term capital formation necessary for infrastructure and industrial growth.
body.hi: The money market, regulated by the RBI, deals with short-term funds (up to one year) and provides liquidity to banks and corporations. In contrast, the capital market, regulated by SEBI, facilitates long-term investment through equity and debt instruments. While the money market ensures the smooth functioning of daily cash flows, the capital market enables long-term capital formation necessary for infrastructure and industrial growth.

conclusion.en: Both markets are complementary; the money market provides the necessary liquidity for the financial system, while the capital market drives long-term economic development.
